Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We propose a $32 million class fund, distributed automatically to all identifiable members, plus $6 million in fees and expenses subject to court approval. Any fees not awarded would go to the class. This provides meaningful relief without requiring members to submit claims.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: defense
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We appreciate the automatic-distribution structure and agree it is appropriate given Brightline’s records. We can offer a $28 million class fund plus $5 million in fees, subject to court approval, with any unawarded fees going to the class.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We appreciate your agreement on automatic payments and on directing any unawarded fees to the class. To bridge the gap, we can reduce our fee request to $5 million if Brightline increases the class fund to $30 million. Fees remain subject to court approval.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: defense
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We are close. Brightline can increase the class fund to $29.5 million, with $5 million in fees subject to court approval. Automatic payments and allocation of any unawarded fees to the class remain unchanged.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We accept Brightline’s latest term sheet: a $29.5 million class fund with automatic distribution, plus $5 million in fees and expenses subject to court approval, with any unawarded fees going to the class and no clear-sailing provision.

Whitcombe Reyes LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Whitcombe Reyes LLP.message: We propose a $36 million class fund distributed automatically using Brightline’s records, plus $6 million in attorneys’ fees and expenses, subject to court approval. Any fees the court does not award would go to the class. Automatic distribution is important here because Brightline can identify the members and their payment cards.

Whitcombe Reyes LLP.speaker: defense
Whitcombe Reyes LLP.message: The proposed $42 million total exceeds our settlement authority. We can offer a $28 million class fund plus $5 million in fees, subject to court approval, with automatic distribution and any unawarded fees going to the class.

Whitcombe Reyes LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Whitcombe Reyes LLP.message: We appreciate Brightline’s movement and its agreement to automatic payments and to directing any unawarded fees to the class. To bridge the remaining gap, we propose a $31 million class fund with $5 million in fees and expenses, subject to court approval, on those same terms.

Whitcombe Reyes LLP.speaker: defense
Whitcombe Reyes LLP.message: We agree on automatic distribution and directing any unawarded fees to the class. Brightline can increase its offer to a $29 million class fund plus $5 million in fees, subject to court approval.

Whitcombe Reyes LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Whitcombe Reyes LLP.message: We appreciate Brightline’s movement. We can narrow the remaining gap with a $30 million class fund and $5 million in fees and expenses, subject to court approval. Payments would be automatic, and any fees not awarded would go to the class.

private_notes.private_reasoning: Open with a substantial class recovery and automatic distribution, since Brightline can identify and pay every member. Keep fees separate, subject to court approval, and direct any unawarded amount to the class. The opening demand leaves room to negotiate without sacrificing those protections.

Open with a substantial automatic-distribution fund reflecting the $64 million in disputed charges, while leaving room to negotiate given certification risk and delay. Keep fees separate and subject to court approval; any reduction should benefit the class, not Brightline.

Hargrove's $38 million proposal is within authority and offers a credible path to approval, but there is room to negotiate a lower total. Whitcombe's $42 million proposal exceeds authority. Preserve automatic distribution and avoid fee arrangements that could jeopardize approval.

The $28 million automatic class fund is substantial, but there is room to improve class recovery. I will counter at $30 million while retaining the defense's $5 million fee figure and class-favorable treatment of any unawarded fees.

The $28 million automatic class fund is a serious offer, especially given certification risk and the delay and uncertainty of trial. A modest counter may improve class recovery without changing the fee or distribution terms. We should not trade automatic payments or class access to unawarded fees for a higher nominal settlement.

Both offers are within authority and provide meaningful automatic relief. A modest counteroffer may reduce Brightline’s outlay while retaining a strong prospect of approval; avoid fee arrangements that could undermine approval.

The $29.5 million fund exceeds the $27.5 million probability-weighted trial award before accounting for certification risk, delay, and litigation costs. Automatic distribution protects class members, and any unawarded fees go to the class. The $5 million fee remains subject to court approval. The remaining $500,000 gap does not justify risking this favorable settlement.

The $29 million fund is a substantial offer, but a $1 million gap remains from a reasonable midpoint. With four rounds left, propose $30 million while preserving automatic distribution and fee protections. The fee remains subject to court approval.

declaration.negotiation_history_statement: The settlement resulted from arm’s-length negotiations with defense counsel. Because the negotiations were confidential mediation communications, I do not recount their exchanges here. The proposed settlement provides a $29.5 million class fund for automatic distribution to approximately 400,000 identifiable members, without a claims process. Brightline will separately pay up to $5 million in attorneys’ fees and expenses, subject to court approval; any amount not awarded will go to the class. There is no clear-sailing provision. In counsel’s judgment, the certain recovery and direct distribution compare favorably with the risks of class certification and trial and the delay of continued litigation. The parties request preliminary approval, subject to notice and the Court’s final fairness review.
